extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers, sports fans, and sports reporters/editors
extracted.subtask_description: Writing concise newspaper game recaps and sports results (box scores, play-by-play, event summaries) across sports such as baseball, football, swimming, track, hockey, etc., as exemplified by early-20th-century daily reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include standard baseball box-score statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the conventional box-score lines: two-base hits, home runs, stolen bases, sacrifice, double plays, left on bases, bases on balls, strikeouts, hits allowed by pitcher, wild pitch, losing pitcher, umpires, time of game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording from page: "Two-Base Hits —Bregsler, Hargrave. Home Run—Hornsby. Stolen Bases—Lindstrom, Zitzmann. Sacrifice—Lucas. Double Plays—Christensen and Pipp; Hornsby, Jackson and Terry. Left on Bases—New York, 3; Cincinnati, 7. Bases on Balls—Off Benton, 1; Luque, 1. Struck Out—By Benton, 4; Luque, 1; Nehf, 1. Hits—Off Luque, 10 in 6 innings; Nehf, 1 in 2. Wild Pitch—Luque. Losing Pitcher—Luque. Umpires—Reardon, O'Day and Moran. Time of Game—2.11." Use these lines verbatim or equivalent concise labels so readers can quickly scan key stats.

rubrics_metrics.name: List starting lineups with positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the starting lineup for each team, showing player name and position (and batting order if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from page: a two-column lineup block labelled by team: "BRAVES  J. Smith, cf. Maguire, 2b. Sisler, 1b. ..." Follow the lineup with attendance and umpire lines (e.g., "Umpires—Stark, Rigler and Hart. Attendance—25,001.").

rubrics_metrics.name: Inning-by-inning (or period-by-period) play-by-play
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrate the game in chronological chunks (by inning, quarter, period), describing key plays, outs, hits and scoring sequences under clear subheadings (e.g., 'First Inning', 'Second Inning').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: section headings like "First Inning" followed by "BRAVES—Lindstrom threw out J. Smith after a fine pickup. Maguire dropped a single..." Use this structure for clarity and to allow readers to follow how the game progressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include attendance and officiating crew
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the game's attendance and name the officials (umpires, referees, linesmen, field judge, head linesman) associated with the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on page: "Attendance—25,001." "Umpires—Reardon, O'Day and Moran." For other sports list referee and assistants (e.g., football: "Referee—Masker, Northwestern. Umpire—Haines, Yale. Field judge—Young, Illinois Wesleyan. Linesman—Huston, Parsons.").

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide scoring-by-period summaries and scoring statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a period-by-period scoring line (quarter/period breakdown) and list scoring plays and point-after details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from football: "SCORE BY PERIODS  Mich 0 7 7 7—21  Ohio State 0 0 0 0—0. Touchdowns—Gilbert (3). Points after touchdowns—Gilbert (3, place kicks)." Use this to let readers see scoring flow at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: List substitutions and roster changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Record substitutions, reserves used, and positional changes for each team during or after the game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: football substitutions block such as "Substitutions—Michigan: Sullo for Parker, Parker for Baer..." and similar lists for soccer, hockey, lacrosse, etc. Include the player names and the players they replaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize notable plays and descriptive color
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short, vivid descriptions of key plays and player actions to give readers a sense of the contest's turning points and atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the copy: descriptive passages such as "Oosterbaan, poised on the Ohio 38-yard line with the ball in his hand, threw straight as a die to Gilbert..." or "The red tipped blades bit into the water..." Use sensory verbs and concise scene-setting to enliven the recap without excess prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-by-event results for track, swimming, and individual events
rubrics_metrics.description: For meets, list each event's placings (first, second, third), times/distances, and note which team or athlete won each event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: "50 Yards Free Style—Won by Teaf, Penn; second, Litchfield, Brown; third, Barrows, Brown. Time—0:25 1-5." Repeat for each event; include relays and any changes due to protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note records, meet/dual/collegiate records, and new bests
rubrics_metrics.description: When a performance sets or equals a record, explicitly state that it is a 'new meet record', 'new collegiate record', or note ties/equalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "Wright tossed the thirty-five-pound weight 55 feet 7% inch, to set a new collegiate and dual meet record." Tag records clearly so the significance is obvious to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report officiating decisions and protests affecting results
rubrics_metrics.description: If an official ruling, protest, or replay changes a result (e.g., relay protests), describe the dispute and the final ruling and how it altered the score or placing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from swimming: explanation of a relay protest—"It was claimed ... that Captain Litchfield started too quickly ... Referee Agnew McBride ordered the relay race recontested. Coach ... would not agree to this, and McBride then awarded the race to Penn, thus making the final score 34 to 28 in Penn’s favor." Include the sequence and final outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise summary headline and lead with location/date/agency tag
rubrics_metrics.description: Start articles with a terse lead that includes the location, date, and wire service or newspaper tag, followed by the essential outcome (final score/result).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "POLO GROUNDS, April 27 (A. P.)—Having lost to the Braves yesterday the Giants had an opportunity..." or "ANN ARBOR, Mich, Oct. 22—Michigan dedicated its $2,000,000 stadium... and crushed Ohio State, 21 to 0..." This orients the reader immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bout/match summaries for boxing, wrestling, fencing, tennis
rubrics_metrics.description: For individual-match sports, give winner/loser, method (e.g., pin, referee's decision, points), round or time if relevant, and short context about fighters/competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: boxing: "Jimmy Maloney ... had little trouble grinding him ..." wrestling: weight-class results with methods and durations (e.g., "158-pound class—Graham, Princeton, threw Carlsten, Columbia, in 3 minutes 12 seconds"). For fencing and tennis provide match scores and notable points or exhibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include final tallies, standings and league tables where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting league sports, include up-to-date standings, points, wins/losses, goals for/against or other tabular summary so readers can place results in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example present: the "AMERICAN LEAGUE STANDING" table and a short list of "Yesterday's Results." Present tidy tables or compact lists for easy reference.
